rows.citation: Melting point 1234.93 K: H. Preston-Thomas, 'The International Temperature Scale of 1990 (ITS-90)', Metrologia 27 (1990) 3-10, doi:10.1088/0026-1394/27/1/002, defining fixed point (freezing point at 101.325 kPa). Boiling point: no primary value was found and none is claimed.

rows.citation: Melting point 184.67 K: K. K. Kelley, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 51 (1929) 1145-1150, doi:10.1021/ja01379a022 (carried over from the primary citation already recorded for this species' enthalpy of fusion in phase_route::FUSION_ENTHALPIES; not re-read against the paper in this lane). Normal boiling point 355.39 K: COMPUTED, not tabulated: the temperature at which the vapour-pressure fit this repository already ships (kerotakis-thermo pack, D. R. Stull, 'Vapor pressure of pure substances: organic compounds', Ind. Eng. Chem. 39 (1947) 517-540, doi:10.1021/ie50448a022, lane pending review) reaches 101.325 kPa, log10(P/bar) = 4.8610 - 1357.427/(T/K - 75.814), solved at P = 1.01325 bar.

Melting point 189.3 K: G. S. Parks, H. M. Huffman and M. Barmore, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 55 (1933) 2733-2740, doi:10.1021/ja01334a016 (carried over from the primary citation already recorded for this species' enthalpy of fusion in phase_route::FUSION_ENTHALPIES; not re-read against the paper in this lane). Boiling point: no primary value was found and none is claimed.

Triple-point (melting) temperature 63.151 K and normal boiling point 77.355 K: R. Span, E. W. Lemmon, R. T. Jacobsen, W. Wagner and A. Yokozeki, 'A reference equation of state for the thermodynamic properties of nitrogen for temperatures from 63.151 to 1000 K and pressures to 2200 MPa', J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 29 (2000) 1361-1433, doi:10.1063/1.1349047. The triple point is in the title; the normal boiling point is recalled from the paper and PENDING REVIEW.

Melting point 175.26 K and normal boiling point 337.9 K (64.7 degrees Celsius): F. D. Rossini, D. D. Wagman, W. H. Evans, S. Levine and I. Jaffe, Selected Values of Chemical Thermodynamic Properties, National Bureau of Standards Circular 500 (1952), phase-transition tables; https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/circ/nbscircular500.pdf, a United States Government work in the public domain (no doi). Read 2026-11-11 through the scanned text layer, which drops substance names from the value lines: the row was identified by its position in the formula-ordered block, so a reviewer should confirm it against the page image. The melting value is the one Circular 500 prints beside methanol's enthalpy of fusion; the primary measurement behind it is K. K. Kelley, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 51 (1929) 180, doi:10.1021/ja01376a022.

Melting point 353.40 K: J. P. McCullough, H. L. Finke, J. F. Messerly, S. S. Todd, T. C. Kincheloe and G. Waddington, J. Phys. Chem. 61 (1957) 1105-1116, doi:10.1021/j150554a016 (carried over from the primary citation already recorded for this species' enthalpy of fusion in phase_route::FUSION_ENTHALPIES; not re-read against the paper in this lane). Boiling point: no primary value was found and none is claimed.

Melting point 177.6 K: G. S. Parks and K. K. Kelley, J. Phys. Chem. 32 (1928) 734-737, doi:10.1021/j150287a006 (carried over from the primary citation already recorded for this species' enthalpy of fusion in phase_route::FUSION_ENTHALPIES; not re-read against the paper in this lane). Normal boiling point 329.34 K: COMPUTED, not tabulated: the temperature at which the vapour-pressure fit this repository already ships (kerotakis-thermo pack, D. R. Stull, 'Vapor pressure of pure substances: organic compounds', Ind. Eng. Chem. 39 (1947) 517-540, doi:10.1021/ie50448a022, lane pending review) reaches 101.325 kPa, log10(P/mmHg) = 7.02447 - 1161.0/(t/degC + 224.0), solved at P = 760 mmHg.

Melting point 298.97 K (stable crystal to liquid): F. L. Oetting, J. Phys. Chem. 67 (1963) 2757-2761, doi:10.1021/j100806a061 (carried over from the primary citation already recorded for this species' enthalpy of fusion in phase_route::FUSION_ENTHALPIES; not re-read against the paper in this lane; PENDING REVIEW). Boiling point: the primary determination (D. Ambrose and C. H. S. Sprake, J. Chem. Thermodyn. 2 (1970) 631, doi:10.1016/0021-9614(70)90038-8) was identified but could not be read, so none is claimed.

Melting 273.15 K and normal boiling 373.15 K: the solvent model's constants (states::WATER_FREEZING_K, WATER_BOILING_K), which the apparatus must agree with. The primary values are 273.1525 K for melting at 101.325 kPa (W. Wagner, T. Riethmann, R. Feistel and A. H. Harvey, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 40 (2011) 043103, doi:10.1063/1.3657937) and 373.124 K for the normal boiling point on ITS-90 (W. Wagner and A. Pruss, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 31 (2002) 387-535, doi:10.1063/1.1461829); the shipped constants differ from them by 0.003 K and 0.026 K, inside the apparatus's stated 0.5 K, and are kept so the two routes cannot disagree.

NOT A MEASURED TRANSITION AND NO LITERATURE VALUE IS CLAIMED: 473.15 K (200 degrees Celsius) is this bench's model threshold for driving the waters of crystallisation off in phase_route::hydrates, an editorial parameter of the dehydration route. Real dehydration is stepwise through intermediate hydrates and depends on heating rate and water vapour pressure; a primary thermogravimetric source has not been attached yet. Model threshold, kerotakis 2026-11-11 (no doi; not a literature citation).
